findings.reason: without a declared wait the queue orders nothing, and this is the same collision class the plan already fixed for §29/§30/§31, so the section must name the edges it needs before it is queued.
findings.text: §32 writes `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py` but declares no wait, and §18, §25, §26, §29 and §31 are all `implementable` and all write that same module, so the queue is free to launch six nodes onto one file at once; the two mechanisms §32 adds (`_retry_backoff_hold` ordering and the pre-`_launch_queued` checks) sit in exactly the region §29 rewrites to record refusal reasons.

findings.reason: §14 is the section that proves the plan and it declares a wait on every sibling precisely so the drain measures the finished queue; omitting the newest implementable section leaves one that the queue will not hold it behind.
findings.text: §14's `plan-section-depends-on` entry lists every other implementable section (§13, §15 and §18–§31) but not §32, so the plan's whole-plan drain measure may be dispatched before the pass-cost section it is meant to cover has landed.

findings.reason: this is the existing judge's constraint, the failure is conservative (it holds rather than colliding), and §32's own measurement is on a `main`-integrating project; naming the integration ref would be a refinement, not a correction of the section's claim.
findings.text: §32 delegates the claim judgement to `node.claim_disposition`, whose `integration_ref` defaults to `"main"` (`reckon/crew/node.py:1534`, `:1459`); for a project that integrates on `develop` the ancestry comparison cannot run, `unintegrated_claim_work` deliberately reports that as work (`node.py:1500-1506`), and the claim therefore binds for ever, so the new `held-on-claim` hold would become the indefinite hold the section exists to remove.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every symbol §32 names resolves at the cited module: `_retry_backoff_hold` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:811`), `_stamp_failure` (`:849`), `ADMISSION_RETRY_BACKOFF_CAP_SECONDS` (`:74`), `_dependency_guard` (`:719`), `admit_once` (`:2621`), and `claim_disposition` (`reckon/crew/node.py:1534`).

rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the node's products are the new test and the live-store pass record; it names no gate log in a temporary path, and its write path is `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py` plus the new test.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `held-on-claim` and `held-until-changed` join the existing hyphenated verdict vocabulary (`held-by-gate`, `held-on-retry-backoff`, `held-behind-earlier-request`), and the test name states the mechanism rather than a plan label.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated root cause matches the code exactly (the back-off is stamped from the pass start, capped at 600 s, and passes 14–20 minutes apart therefore always clear it), the mechanism is capable of the four arms, and it runs on the named production path (`admit_once` → `_launch_queued`, with the pre-check placed before the launch call).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the claim pre-check, the `held-until-changed` policy and the failure-moment back-off all serve the one measure named by the title (a request that cannot launch costs a pass nothing) and are provable by one dispatch-attempt count.
